Det bleggule hatkød er ret blånende. Sporerne har utydelige længdestriber og måler 12,5-14 x 4,5-5 μm, Q-gns 2,9. Med løvtræer, fx pil, på fugtige voksesteder.
attributes.forvekslingsmuligheder: Ligner mest en lille blodrød rørhat (Hortiboletus rubellus), men denne har i reglen orange korn i stokbasis, vokser mere parkagtigt og har bredere sporer, Q-gns 2,3. Xerocomellus fennicus ligner på næsten alle måder, men har 5-100% trunkerede sporer, der er en smule smallere, Q-gns 2,6. Den er kendt fra enkelte danske fund.
attributes.oekologi: Boletus ripariellus er fundet én gang i Danmark, i en klit med krybende pil (Salix repens ssp. repens var. repens) på Fanø i 1990.

attributes.bogtekst_gyldendal_en:
Xerocomellus ripariellus is a very small to small bolete with a finely felty, blood-red, rarely deep orange-brown, white-cracking cap and pale yellow, quickly bluing pores. The yellowish stem is covered in coral-red dots and fibres. The pale yellow flesh stains blue in both cap and stem and lacks orange grains. The spores have indistinct ridges/stripes and measure 12.5–14 × 4.5–5 µm, Qav. 2.9. Occurs with deciduous trees, e.g. Salix and Alnus, in damp habitats.
Recalls a small Hortiboletus rubellus but that species has orange grains in the stem base, occurs in parklands and has wider spores with a Qav. of 2.3. Xerocomellus fennicus is very similar but 5–100% of the spores are truncate and they are somewhat narrower (Qav. 2.6). Rheubarbariboletus armeniacus also lacks coloured grains in the stem base but is rather larger and the cap cuticle hyphae have red spots in Congo Red.
Widespread, but apparently very rare; July–October.
